# Results -- Study 294 (Coinbase-Rank) on the real BTC/ETH tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: around each
hardcoded "Coinbase app spiked toward #1 in the App Store" date, fit a market
model `BTC = a + b*ETH` on non-event days, measure BTC's **forward** abnormal
return over [+1, +5] (the omen is a contrarian top, so we look at the days AFTER
the spike), and confront it with an honest, one-day-lagged SHORT backtest that
pays fees and borrow. Pinned against a permutation null and a synthetic positive
control. **Hindsight-selected**: the spike list is the set of FAMOUS "Coinbase hit
#1" moments -- remembered because a top often followed -- so all results are an
upper bound on the omen. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (btc_ret) |
|--------|--------|-------|----------------------|
| yfinance BTC-USD / ETH-USD daily (auto-adj close) | 2017-11-10 -> 2026-06-17 | 3142 daily returns | `fcd0c13455df` |

Events: 15 hardcoded Coinbase App-Store rank spikes (2017-2025), all tagged +1
(retail-euphoria "toward #1" markers).

## Primary specification (forward event study, market model on ETH)

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Market-model beta on ETH | 0.605 |
| Day-0 abnormal return (spike-day reaction) | **+2.29%** (a final up-thrust) |
| **Forward CAR [+1, +5]** | **-5.23%** |
| Cross-sectional t (forward CAR) | **-1.69** |
| Permutation p (forward CAR, two-sided) | **0.0014** |
| Negative events (omen "worked") | **8 / 15** |

- The forward CAR points the way the omen predicts (BTC weakens after the spike),
  and the **permutation p is small (~0.001)** -- but the permutation mean is
  driven by a couple of large crashes. The **cross-sectional t = -1.69 does NOT
  clear the |2| bar**, which is the robust hurdle. Per the desk rubric, that makes
  the signal **WEAK**, not REAL.

## Robustness -- one or two crashes do the work

| Spec | Forward CAR | t |
|------|-------------|---|
| All 15 events (raw) | -5.23% | **-1.69** |
| Drop single worst event | -3.53% | **-1.27** |
| Median event | **-0.97%** | -- |

Dropping the single most-negative event (a real blow-off) cuts the mean and pushes
the t toward zero; the *median* event is nearly flat. Only **8/15** events were even
negative -- barely above a coin. **The signal is fragile, not robust.**

## Forward-horizon sweep

| Horizon | Forward CAR | t | perm p |
|---------|-------------|---|--------|
| [+1, +3] | -2.87% | -1.29 | 0.0148 |
| **[+1, +5]** | **-5.23%** | **-1.69** | **0.0014** |
| [+1, +10] | -4.75% | -1.55 | 0.0186 |

No horizon clears |t| >= 2; the effect is directionally consistent but
sub-threshold across the board.

## Tradability -- the lagged SHORT backtest (one-day lag, fees + borrow)

SHORT BTC at the spike-day close (one honest day of lag), hold `h` days, pay 20 bps
one-way on entry/exit against NAV **plus** 5 bps/day borrow. A positive net means
the short made money (BTC fell).

| Hold | Net short / trade | BTC long / trade | Net t | Hit-rate |
|------|-------------------|------------------|-------|----------|
| 3d | +2.39% | -2.94% | +1.10 | 60% |
| **5d** | **+2.37%** | **-3.02%** | **+0.80** | **53%** |
| 10d | -0.40% | -0.50% | -0.08 | 40% |

The short is roughly break-even-to-mildly-positive only because BTC genuinely
averaged a loss over these (hindsight-selected) windows -- but the **net t <= ~1
and the hit-rate hovers at ~50%** at every horizon. Shorting the strongest-trending
major asset on a sub-2-sigma, coin-flip signal -- with borrow ticking daily -- is a
negative-expectancy trade. **No harvestable edge.**

## Positive control -- the machinery finds a planted drift

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`), the same forward
event-study engine recovers a planted post-spike negative drift monotonically:

| Planted drift (bps/day) | Forward CAR | t | perm p |
|-------------------------|-------------|---|--------|
| 0 (null) | +1.2% | +0.68 | 0.516 |
| 200 | -8.3% | -4.77 | 0.000 |
| 500 | -22.5% | -12.9 | 0.000 |
| 1000 | -46.2% | -26.4 | 0.000 |

The engine is quiet at the null and detects a real drift cleanly (|t| >> 2). So the
real-tape verdict -- a **weak, directionally-correct** drag that is **un-tradable**
-- is a statement about BTC and the tiny, hindsight-selected event set, not about
the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** Forward CAR = -5.23% points the omen's way and the
  permutation p (~0.001) looks compelling, **but** the robust cross-sectional t is
  only **-1.69** (< |2|), only **8/15** events are negative, the median event is
  **-0.97%**, and dropping one crash collapses it (t -> -1.27). On a
  hindsight-selected list of 15 events, that is a *whisper*, not a real signal --
  and literature/behavioural support alone keeps it at WEAK, not REAL.
  Survivorship/selection bias named here.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** After a one-day lag, fees, and borrow, the short nets
  **+2.4%/trade** with **t = 0.80** and a **53%** hit-rate -- a coin flip. Shorting
  a structurally up-trending asset on this signal loses money in expectation. No
  tradable vehicle survives the honest frictions.
- **Hindsight -- named.** The spike list is the set of famous "Coinbase hit #1"
  moments, remembered precisely because a top often followed. All numbers above are
  an **upper bound** on the omen's true forward forecasting power.
